# Results — Study 618 (GBTC Premium Cycle)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **GBTC
traded ~40 % ABOVE its bitcoin, then ~45 % below, then snapped to zero the day it became an
ETF: one wrapper, three regimes, all mechanical** — measured on a premium series reconstructed
from public trust mechanics (inception ratio 0.1 BTC/share, 2 %/yr fee accrued in BTC, 91-for-1
split, 1.5 %/yr fee + in-kind arb after the 2024-01-11 ETF conversion, ×0.90 Mini-Trust
spin-off factor). Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (last complete month). Fingerprint `5ffd3440484c`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes: **GBTC** (split/spin-off-adjusted) + **BTC-USD**, aligned on GBTC trading days |
| Window | 2015-05-11 → 2026-06-30 (**2,801** days; GBTC's first OTCQX print to as-of) |
| Premium | `GBTC / (BTC × modeled BTC-per-share) − 1`; model anchors match Grayscale's disclosed ratios (0.0010076 vs ~0.00101 at the 2018 split; 0.00089442 vs ~0.00089 at conversion) |
| Self-validation | ETF-era premium (arb-enforced ≈ 0) reads mean **−0.026 %**, sd 0.915 % — the model matches the arbitraged NAV to ~3 bp |
| Execution / costs | ONE documented lag: the convergence trade enters at the close **one trading day after** BlackRock's 2023-06-15 filing; costs 10/25/50 bps one-way × 4 legs; the short-BTC leg pays **5 %/yr** borrow/roll carry |
| Timing caveat | BTC-USD closes ~00:00 UTC vs GBTC 16:00 ET — a few hours of mismatch adds noise (sd) to the daily premium, not bias |

*No survivorship issue: a single named vehicle followed through its whole life, including the
regime that killed its imitators.*

## Three regimes, one wrapper (premium level; HAC lag = 63 days on the level)

| regime | window | n | mean | HAC *t* | extreme |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| **Premium era** | 2015-05-11 → 2021-02-22 | 1,457 | **+36.32 %** | **+8.97** | peak **+132.01 %** (2017-08-31) |
| **Discount era** | 2021-02-23 → 2024-01-10 | 726 | **−24.49 %** | **−7.44** | trough **−48.80 %** (2022-12-13) |
| **ETF era** | 2024-01-11 → 2026-06-30 | 618 | **−0.03 %** | −0.85 | min −4.11 % / max +5.38 % |

- First sustained discount (5 straight closes below NAV): **2021-02-26** — the flip is a dated,
  one-way event, not a fluctuation.
- Premium-era vs discount-era daily premium: **Welch *t* = +80.23** (the two regimes are
  different planets).
- ETF era = the calibration residual: mean **−0.026 %**, mean |premium| **0.638 %** — the
  in-kind create/redeem arb pins price to NAV, and our reconstruction sits on it to basis
  points. The level *t*'s carry a caveat: the premium is highly persistent inside a regime, so
  even the 63-day HAC lag understates the true level uncertainty — the decisive inference lives
  on the **drift** below.

## The dated trade — the 2023 discount convergence (long GBTC / short BTC = d log(1+prem))

| window | days | premium path | total drift | bps/day | HAC(10) *t* |
|---|--:|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Full 2023 (2023-01-03 → 2024-01-11) | 257 | −45.95 % → −1.52 % | **+59.99 log-pts** | +23.34 | **+1.92** |
| **Ex-ante trigger** (enter close 2023-06-16, one trading day after BlackRock's filing; exit conversion close 2024-01-11) | 143 | −36.29 % → −1.52 % | **+43.54 log-pts** | +30.45 | **+2.69** |

The full-calendar-2023 window (a window only hindsight would pick) reads HAC *t* = 1.92 — we
say so. The **honest, ex-ante version** — enter the day after a public, dated catalyst
(BlackRock's S-1, the first credible spot-ETF sponsor), exit at the conversion — clears the bar
at **HAC *t* = +2.69**, forgoing the entire first-day pop by construction.

### Event days (one-day hedged move, z vs discount-era daily sd)

| date | event | move | z |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| 2023-06-15 | BlackRock files the iShares spot-BTC ETF (after hours) | −0.73 % | −0.3 |
| 2023-06-16 | first close AFTER the filing | **+9.19 %** | **+3.5** |
| 2023-08-29 | *Grayscale v. SEC* — DC Circuit vacates the denial | **+9.64 %** | **+3.7** |
| 2024-01-10 | SEC approves spot bitcoin ETFs | +2.72 % | +1.0 |
| 2024-01-11 | GBTC's first day as a spot ETF | +1.04 % | +0.4 |

The two legal/filing catalysts are **3.5–3.7 sd** one-day moves on the hedged book; the
approval itself was already ~priced (the discount was −2.5 % by 2024-01-10).

| one-way cost | gross | legs | borrow (5 %/yr) | net (simple) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps | +43.54 log-pts | 0.40 pp | 2.84 pp | **+49.63 %** |
| 25 bps | +43.54 log-pts | 1.00 pp | 2.84 pp | **+48.74 %** |
| 50 bps | +43.54 log-pts | 2.00 pp | 2.84 pp | **+47.26 %** |

Costs are a rounding error against a 43-log-pt bounded convergence with a terminal event. The
vehicle was retail-accessible (GBTC in any brokerage; the hedge via CME micro futures or BITO).
Capacity was billions (GBTC held ~$25B at conversion). **But the trade no longer exists** —
the ETF era premium is ≈ 0 and the wrapper arb is structurally closed.

## Third axis — who could harvest each regime? (the accredited create-and-dump arb)

Premium-era creations were **private-placement only** (accredited investors, Reg D), created at
NAV and saleable only after the Rule-144 lockup (6 months from Oct-2019, **12 months before** —
we charge the favourable 126 trading days). Hedged net P&L per monthly cohort (fee drag +
3 legs × 25 bps + 5 %/yr borrow):

| cohort group | n | mean net (log-pts) | worst | share > 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| created 2015-06 … 2020-08 (premium era) | 63 | **+26.49** | −1.98 | **98 %** |
| created 2020-09 … 2021-06 (exit into the flip) | 10 | **−16.96** | **−23.03** | 0 % |

Early-vs-late Welch *t* = **+17.76**. The create-and-dump printed ~+26 log-pts per 6-month
lockup with a 98 % hit rate for five years — for accredited investors only; the public could
only *pay* the premium (that demand is what the arb was dumping into). Then the same trade,
same mechanics, lost ~17–23 log-pts per cohort the moment the regime flipped mid-lockup — the
"riskless" carry that helped sink Three Arrows Capital and BlockFi. The one leg the public
could genuinely harvest was the **2023 discount convergence** (any brokerage). After
2024-01-11, nobody harvests anything: the arb *is* the ETF.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is faithful

Planted three-regime world (plateau +40 %, trough −45 %, tunable convergence drift into a
known conversion date) plus a null whose premium is AR(1) noise around zero:

| world | plateau mean read | conv-window HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| planted premium + convergence drift | +41.05 % | **+3.37** |
| planted premium, NO drift | +41.05 % | +0.29 |
| null (premium ≈ 0 throughout) | +0.75 % | +0.29 |

Levels are recovered, the HAC *t* lights up only when a drift is actually planted, and the null
does not manufacture significance. *(Machinery proof only — never cited in support of a
stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** All three regimes are on the tape with robust statistics: premium era
  **+36.32 %** (HAC *t* = +8.97), discount era **−24.49 %** (HAC *t* = −7.44), Welch *t* = 80
  between them; the dated 2023 convergence clears the bar on its honest ex-ante version
  (**HAC *t* = +2.69**, +43.5 log-pts after a one-day lag) with 3.5–3.7 sd event days on the
  two documented catalysts; and the ETF era sits at **−0.03 %** exactly as the arb demands.
  (Full-calendar-2023, the hindsight window, reads *t* = 1.92 — reported as such.)
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The convergence leg was genuinely deployable — retail-accessible,
  billions of capacity, **+49.6 % net** of costs and borrow in 7 months — but it was a
  **one-shot, dated trade that no longer exists**: the ETF conversion killed the wrapper arb
  permanently (ETF-era |premium| averages 0.6 %). The premium-era leg was never deployable by
  the public at all.
- **Who could harvest each regime? — MIXED.** Premium era: **accredited only** (create-and-dump,
  +26 log-pts/cohort, 98 % hit rate — until the flip turned it into −17 to −23); public
  investors could only pay the premium. Discount era: **anyone with a brokerage** (the one
  public leg). ETF era: **no one** — the arbitrage became the product.
